routes.name: Monroe Brook Slide
routes.approach: Start at the Cog Railway lot, take the Ammonoosuc Link to the Ammonoosuc Ravine Trail, and follow the river on the flat, narrow trail until a small tributary crosses it. The stream is hard to spot unless there are tracks. Leave the trail there on your right, climb through open conifer glades to the foot of the slide, then follow the easy snow gully uphill. routes.name: Chute, The

routes.descent: The top rolls over almost flat. Mountaineers heading for the summit or coming back should descend the Lion Head Winter Route, or downclimb Right Gully to the ravine floor. A slip here can slide a long way, so be sure of your axe and crampons.

routes.name: Lion's Head Gully
routes.approach: Begin at the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center on Route 16 and hike up the Tuckerman Ravine Trail as far as the Hermit Lake Shelter, with the whole ravine in view from there; the trail continues to the floor of the bowl. The route is the narrow gully right of Lobster Claw, reached by a faint runout path through bushes to its base. It does not always fill in. All of Tuckerman's lines lie below big snow
routes.descent: The gully ends at the Alpine Garden, from which you can cross to the summit by the East Snowfields. Descend by Right Gully or Lobster Claw back to the ravine floor, or take the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.

routes.descent: The gully tops out on the Alpine Garden, where you can continue toward the summit. Descend the way you came, or use the Lion Head Winter Route to the Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
